full_judgment:
3. Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that sub-section 6 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 makes no provision for making the statutory deposit before the final determination of claim of the co-applicant and, as such, the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order arbitrarily. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before us petitioner's application under sub-section 4 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for being added as a co-applicant (co-pre-emptor) and the impugned order passed by the Subordinate Judge allowing the petitioner's application for being added as a co-applicant for pre-emption with a direction to make the statutory deposit promptly. 

 7. Under section 96(6) the co-applicant is required to make the statutory deposit within the time allowed by the Court. Nowhere in the scheme of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it has been spelt out that the co-applicant can make the necessary deposit after the final determination of his claim by the Court. Such an argument appears to be totally misconceived and preposterous. Under sub-section 96(1) of the SAT Act., making the statutory deposit is a condition precedent for filing a pre-emption case but it is not so in case of an application under section 94(4) of the said Act. In the latter case, the co-applicant is required to make the necessary deposit within the time allowed by the Court after his prayer to be joined as a co-applicant has been allowed. If he fails to comply with the deposit within the time given by the Court, his application under section 96(4) of the S.A.T Act would stand rejected.
